etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English rewme, realme, reaume, from Old French reaume, realme (“kingdom”), of unclear origins. A postulated *rēgālimen (“domain, kingdom”), Late Latin or Vulgar Latin cross of regimen with rēgālis is usually cited.

The modern pronunciation with /l/ is either a spelling pronunciation or influenced by the etymology.

definitions.definition: An abstract sphere of influence, real or imagined.

quote.citation: 1907, Tada Kanai, “The World and How to Pass Through It”, in Arthur Lloyd, transl., Seven Buddhist Sermons:
quote.text: Why should we despise anything in the realm of Buddha?

quote.citation: 2006 November 22, Christian Neef, “Diary of a Collapsing Superpower”, in Spiegel Magazine:
quote.text: At home in Moscow, Mikhail Sergeyevitch Gorbachev, who had launched a campaign to rejuvenate the Soviet realm  […]

quote.citation: 2013 May 17, George Monbiot, “Money just makes the rich suffer”, in The Guardian Weekly‎[2], volume 188, number 23, page 19:
quote.text: In order to grant the rich these pleasures, the social contract is reconfigured. […]  The public realm is privatised, the regulations restraining the ultra-wealthy and the companies they control are abandoned, and Edwardian levels of inequality are almost fetishised.

definitions.definition: The domain of a certain abstraction.

quote.citation: 1922, Judson Eber Conant, “Truth Must be Classified Scientifically”, in The Church The Schools and Evolution:
quote.text: One thing more which the scientific man does is to accord primacy to that realm of truth which is primary in importance.

definitions.definition: (computing) A scope of operation in networking or security.
(formal or law) A territory or state, as ruled by a specific power, especially by a king.

quote.citation: 1874, Horatio Alger, “Chapter XXXI”, in Brave and Bold:
quote.text: And, of this island realm, he and his companion were the undisputed sovereigns.

quote.citation: 1913, Leslie Alexander Toke, Catholic Encyclopedia, "St. Dunstan",
quote.text: Then seeing his life was threatened he fled the realm and crossed over to Flanders,  […]

definitions.definition: (fantasy, roleplaying games) An otherworldly dimension or domain — magical, ethereal, or otherwise — usually ruled or created by a mystical character.
(virology, taxonomy) A taxonomic rank in the phylogeny of viruses, higher than kingdoms.
